# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |

| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Make a compact action truthful in every state

Read [the controls guide](../../references/controls.md). This workflow is application advice; preserve platform/locked-device qualifications and verify actual API support in the supplied stack.

Inspect the action or binary state, configuration, security sensitivity, locked/unlocked surfaces, platform, and create/review/adapt request. Identify direct action versus app-opening behavior and the authoritative state source. A tinted symbol alone does not prove the controlled device changed.

Choose useful focused work, preferably avoiding an app launch. Supply a symbol understandable without text because some surfaces omit labels, plus title/value for larger presentations. Keep state accurate after interaction, completion, and remote changes; distinguish ongoing duration from confirmed completion. Configure required parameters when added and allow later changes. Redact private titles/values while locked and require authentication for security-sensitive actions. A locked camera experience is capture-only until unlocking for further work; preserve UI continuity. Do not promise Controls on watchOS/tvOS/visionOS.

Implement the control/configuration/state binding or provide an action-state/authentication contract; reviews identify exact wrong-state or locked-disclosure defects. Keep a proposed UI change separate from unverified access-control enforcement.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a garage control displays “Open” immediately on press, leaks the home name while locked, and never reflects a remote close. Decision: request acceptance differs from device state and locked text is private. After: expose an understandable symbol, authenticated action, pending/confirmed behavior, redacted text, and updates from authoritative remote changes.

Deliver the artifact, surface variants, configuration, authoritative state, and locked/auth rules. Verify remote change, failed action, reconfiguration, locked state, and symbol-only comprehension. Fail for falsely confirmed state, unauthenticated sensitive action, or private locked text. Report native Control Center/Action-button/security execution separately from logic inspection.

Load [widgets](../apple-hig-widgets/SKILL.md) for information, [live-activities](../apple-hig-live-activities/SKILL.md) for bounded progress, or [privacy](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-privacy/SKILL.md) for sensitive handling.

# Controls Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/controls) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Controls expose an app button or binary toggle in Control Center, Lock Screen, or the Action button. Buttons can act, open a specific destination, or launch a locked-device camera. People add them through Control Center editing, Lock Screen customization, or Action button settings. ## Anatomy Provide a meaningful SF/custom symbol, a title, and optional state value. Larger Control Center sizes show text; Lock Screen uses only the symbol; Action-button activation can show symbol and value in Dynamic Island. The symbol therefore must communicate purpose without labels. ## Best practices Favor useful actions that avoid launching the app, such as starting a Live Activity. Update after interaction, completion, and remote changes so displayed state and progress remain accurate. Supply meaningful symbols for both toggle states, animate their transitions, and animate a duration-based button while its task remains active. Choose a branded tint for the on symbol and Action-button feedback. Prompt for required configuration when first added, with later reconfiguration available. Provide verb-based press-and-hold hints for Action button use, and illustrative placeholders for variable titles/values in galleries. Redact private title/value text when locked and, if needed, show the symbol's off state too. Require authentication for security-sensitive actions such as doors or vehicle starting. ## Camera experiences on a locked device From iOS 18, a control can open a capture experience while locked. Tasks beyond capture require unlocking and transition into the app. Reuse the app's camera UI for a familiar seamless transition, and explain how to add the camera control. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, or macOS rules are specified. Controls are unsupported in watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Widgets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets) [Action button](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/action-button) #### Developer documentation ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 10, 2024.

# Ask for precise access when its purpose is clear

Read [Privacy](../../references/privacy.md). Inspect the feature's actual data needs, transfers, storage, current permission flow, and supported platform. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Produce the requested copy/flow/data-handling changes in the existing stack; distinguish documented platform restrictions from additional application recommendations.

Map each requested category to a specific feature and minimum necessary scope. Remove collection without a concrete benefit; prefer on-device work where it avoids unnecessary transfer. Explain collection/use accurately and flag App Store disclosure updates needed when behavior changes. Respect private email and tracking choices rather than designing around them.

Ask when the person invokes the feature. Launch-time requests need an essential, obvious dependency. Write a short active purpose sentence explaining use and reason. If context is sufficient, omit a custom pre-alert; if explanation is essential, use one clear continuation to the real system alert without imitating Allow/Don't Allow. Keep the guide's special pre-alert restrictions distinct from ordinary onboarding. Tracking requires its system authorization before collection and must not be incentivized or manipulated.

Choose one-time location access for suitable individual tasks using the system location button on supported platforms; preserve permitted customization and all localized/accessibility-sized text. Protect secrets with established authentication/keychain mechanisms. For Mac, account for sandboxing/distribution and fast user switching. For visionOS, separate system rendering assistance from permission-gated Full Space ARKit data; gaze remains private, and imported phone-camera assumptions may need removal or content import.

**Before → decision → after:** A bird journal asks for contacts, microphone, and continuous location at launch although only “Attach current location” uses location. Decision: request only the specific action's needed access. After, journaling works immediately; the attachment action offers the supported location control, and its purpose explains adding the sighting's location.

Deliver a data-purpose/access matrix and corrected permission sequence/copy or implementation. Fail if collection precedes required consent, copy obscures the real use, or unrelated work is gated on optional access. Report code/flow evidence separately from actual authorization prompts and privacy-setting behavior; this procedure does not certify security or legal compliance.

Use [Sign in with Apple](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-sign-in-with-apple/SKILL.md) for that authentication choice and [Augmented reality](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-augmented-reality/SKILL.md) when room/camera access is essential.

For health-related work, finish the domain decisions as well as the permission
sequence. Read [CareKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-carekit/SKILL.md)
for care plans, scheduled treatment tasks, or symptom/event recording;
[HealthKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-healthkit/SKILL.md)
for health-data access and sharing; and
[ResearchKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-researchkit/SKILL.md)
for study participation and research consent. These experience procedures help
choose task, data, and consent behavior in the existing stack; consulting a
framework-named topic does not require adopting that SDK. General privacy,
language, and accessibility guidance alone does not resolve those domain choices.

# Privacy Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Communicate collection and usage clearly and protect granted data. Keep App Store privacy disclosures accurate for new releases and updates; people rely on them before downloading. ## Best practices Collect only what the specific feature requires and make access as precise as possible. Respect Hide My Email, Mail Privacy Protection, and tracking choices. Prefer on-device processing, including Create ML/Neural Engine where useful, to avoid unnecessary server transfers. Use system encryption, key management, and established security protections, including CloudKit’s additional encrypted data types where available. ## Requesting permission Protected categories include personal/location/health/financial/contact information, user-created content, messages/calendar/music/gameplay/HomeKit data, media, Bluetooth/Wi-Fi/local network resources, camera/microphone, the advertising identifier, and permission-gated ARKit data in a visionOS Full Space. The system displays the app’s purpose string and stores choices/descriptions in privacy settings. Ask when the person invokes the relevant feature. Request at launch only when access is essential and obviously necessary, such as location for navigation or room information for a spatial game that needs walls. Write a short, specific, active, complete sentence in sentence case with a period, explaining both use and reason. # Expose state rather than disguise an action

Read [the toggle guide](../../references/toggles.md). This procedure is application advice; preserve the source's style and platform distinctions.

Inspect setting meaning, affected content, dependencies, aggregate selection, platform, and create/review/adapt mode. On iOS/iPadOS use switches in labelled list rows and appropriate stateful buttons outside; do not add brand color without a reason. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A toggle controls opposing states, commonly on/off. The system offers styles such as switches and checkboxes, while buttons can also retain toggle state through appearance changes. ## Best practices Use toggles for state, and another component for actions or selection from a list. Identify the affected content through context or an appropriate label. Toggle buttons typically use a meaningful glyph plus a changed background. Make state differences clear through shape, fill, checkmark, or dot; color alone is insufficient. ## Platform considerations No extra tvOS, visionOS, or watchOS rules are specified. ### iOS, iPadOS Use switch-style toggles in list rows where row content supplies the label. Keep the normal green unless a different accent is necessary, and ensure the on appearance contrasts with off. Outside lists, use a stateful button. A familiar icon and obvious state appearance should explain the visible button without an added explanatory label. ### macOS Place switches, checkboxes, and radio buttons in the window body rather than the toolbar or status bar. #### Switches A switch has stronger visual emphasis than a checkbox; use it for prominent settings or enabling an entire settings group. Retain established checkboxes rather than replacing them merely for a new appearance. #### Checkboxes Checkboxes show empty/off, checkmark/on, or dash/mixed states, usually with a trailing title; editable checklists can omit the title. Leading alignment and indentation make checkboxes useful for hierarchical dependencies. A group label can clarify related choices; align its baseline with the first checkbox. Reflect aggregate mixed state when subordinate choices differ. Use radio buttons when more than two choices must be mutually exclusive. #### Radio buttons Radio groups commonly contain 2–5 labeled circles and allow one choice. A mixed state is possible but rarely useful; a checkbox usually communicates mixed state better. Use checkboxes for multiple independent choices or a lone binary setting. A pair of explicit radio labels can help only when a single checkbox cannot explain the opposing meanings. For more than about 5 options, evaluate a pop-up. Supply a recognizable lamp symbol with distinct illuminated/unilluminated forms; color is supplementary. Supply title and state text for sizes that show text. Do not interpret a tinted symbol as device confirmation. [Controls — Anatomy](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/controls#Anatomy), [Toggles — iOS/iPadOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/toggles#iOS-iPadOS).

A separately designed owner-only maintenance flow in the app is outside this specification; merely moving reset is not evidence that its safeguards exist.

This document does not establish minimum OS/API availability. The local Controls guide explicitly excludes watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS; absence of other platform rules does not prove implementation support. ## Configuration and destinations

- Gallery: title “Lamp power”, sample title “Desk lamp”, sample value “Off”, and a lamp symbol. Examples are illustrative, never a live lamp state.

Commit invalidates cached state, cancels local pending work, and reads the new lamp before enabling power. An already-dispatched old-lamp command may still complete; it cannot update the new tile.
- Removed lamp: show “Lamp unavailable”; no power dispatch. Account changes invalidate the binding and require reselection; never reuse a different account's matching ID.
- Recovery destinations, where the surface supports them, open that lamp's status/permission page. Otherwise expose the explanation in configuration and in the app. Opening recovery must be a separate, clearly labeled action, not the power toggle's activation.

Required configuration and later editing follow [Controls — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/controls#Best-practices). Precise destinations and preserved context follow [Designing for iOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios#Best-practices).

Authoritative power comes from a device-confirmed reading/event, with lamp ID, revision/order token, and observation time. A transport acknowledgement only confirms receipt of a request. Reachability and account authorization are separate inputs. No default power value is On.

Product defaults, not Apple mandates: a reading is fresh for 30 seconds while its connection remains healthy; invalidate immediately on disconnection. A command has a 10-second confirmation deadline. These values require validation against the eventual lamp protocol. If ordered events or freshness cannot be established, expose unknown state rather than guess.

| Missing selection | Lamp power / Choose a lamp | No dispatch; configure through editing |
| No account or denied/revoked lamp permission | Lamp power / Access required | No dispatch; app recovery explains sign-in or owner-granted access |

| Offline/disconnected | Selected name / Offline | No dispatch; refresh on reconnect |
| No fresh reading | Selected name / State unavailable | No dispatch; request a read |
| Command awaiting confirmation | Selected name / Turning on… or Turning off… | No second dispatch; coalesce repeated activation |
